### limes.ErrUnauthenticated, limes.ErrInvalidToken, limes.ErrProofOfPossession, limes.ErrExpired, limes.ErrNotYetValid, limes.ErrRevoked, limes.ErrTenantErased, limes.ErrDelegationTooDeep, limes.ErrAudienceMismatch, limes.ErrUnrecorded, limes.ErrCaveatViolation, limes.ErrBudgetExceeded, limes.ErrInvalidAmount, limes.ErrCursorMismatch, limes.ErrRequestLimitExceeded, limes.ErrTenantBudgetExceeded, limes.ErrDelegationTooWide, limes.ErrDelegationDepthExceeded, limes.ErrUnitCodeMismatch, limes.ErrInvalidRequest, limes.ErrInvalidConfig, limes.ErrInternal, limes.ErrUnknownTenant, limes.ErrTenantDeleted, limes.ErrTenantGone, limes.ErrScopeMismatch, limes.ErrProofUnsupported, limes.ErrRevocationUnavailable

```go
var (
	// ErrUnauthenticated is the family of every refusal of the presented
	// credentials, token or proof: the one errors.Is a consumer needs to
	// answer them all as unauthenticated.
	ErrUnauthenticated = errors.New("limes: unauthenticated")
	// ErrInvalidToken — the token is not genuine or not this verifier's
	// to accept: a bad signature, an unknown kid, an untrusted issuer, a
	// malformed header or claims. One sentinel for all, so a caller cannot
	// tell an attacker which check failed.
	ErrInvalidToken error = &familyError{"limes: invalid token", ErrUnauthenticated}
	// ErrProofOfPossession is the family of every proof-of-possession
	// refusal: the token may be genuine, the proof that its holder sent it
	// is what failed. The verifier wraps each dpop refusal in it.
	ErrProofOfPossession error = &familyError{"limes: proof of possession refused", ErrUnauthenticated}
	ErrExpired           error = &familyError{"limes: expired", ErrUnauthenticated}
	ErrNotYetValid       error = &familyError{"limes: not yet valid", ErrUnauthenticated}
	ErrRevoked           error = &familyError{"limes: revoked", ErrUnauthenticated}
	// ErrTenantErased is a metering call, or a Store.Insert, for a tenant
	// whose usage EraseTenantUsage removed: nothing of it is recorded or
	// counted again. Its capabilities were revoked with it, so it matches
	// ErrRevoked. The Issuer answers a mint the store refuses with it as
	// ErrTenantGone instead: no presented capability was refused.
	ErrTenantErased error = &familyError{"limes: tenant erased", ErrRevoked}
	// ErrDelegationTooDeep — a capability with more than MaxDelegationDepth
	// ancestors on record. Its root lies past the bounded IsRevoked walk,
	// so a revocation there would go unseen: it is refused as revoked,
	// never accepted. A store answers it as an error, which no revocation
	// cache keeps. Store.Insert refuses to record one with it, which
	// Delegate answers as ErrDelegationDepthExceeded: the parent is live,
	// only too deep to delegate from.
	ErrDelegationTooDeep error = &familyError{"limes: delegation chain too deep", ErrRevoked}
	ErrAudienceMismatch  error = &familyError{"limes: audience mismatch", ErrUnauthenticated}
	// ErrUnrecorded — a capability the revocation lookup has no record of,
	// refused unless VerifierConfig.AllowUnrecorded is set, rather than read as not
	// revoked: a lookup that cannot see the record could not see its
	// revocation either. It is not ErrRevoked, so an operator tells a
	// lookup blind to an issuer's records, or a store restored from an older
	// backup, from a capability someone stopped.
	ErrUnrecorded      error = &familyError{"limes: capability not on record", ErrUnauthenticated}
	ErrCaveatViolation       = errors.New("limes: caveat violation")
	ErrBudgetExceeded        = errors.New("limes: budget exceeded")

	// ErrInvalidAmount — an amount that is negative or above MaxNanos, a
	// decimal that is not one or is finer than a nano (ParseAmount), a float
	// that is not a number (AmountFromFloat), or JSON that is not a string.
	// Refunds are explicit; a negative charge is not one. A malformed request, so it matches
	// ErrInvalidRequest.
	ErrInvalidAmount error = &familyError{"limes: invalid amount", ErrInvalidRequest}

	// ErrCursorMismatch — a cursor RecordLister.ListRecords handed out for
	// another order, tenant or other filters, handed back with these: well formed,
	// but a place in another listing. A caller that tells it from a
	// malformed request starts again from the first page. It matches
	// ErrInvalidRequest, as every refused request does; a cursor that is
	// not one at all is ErrInvalidRequest alone.
	ErrCursorMismatch error = &familyError{"limes: cursor of another listing", ErrInvalidRequest}

	// ErrRequestLimitExceeded — the capability, a Biscuit copy or an
	// ancestor used every request its ceiling allows; the next was blocked.
	ErrRequestLimitExceeded = errors.New("limes: request limit exceeded")

	// ErrTenantBudgetExceeded — the tenant aggregate cap has been
	// hit. Distinct from ErrBudgetExceeded because the remedy differs:
	// an operator raises a tenant's ceiling with SetTenantBudget, while a
	// capability's ceiling is in its token and lifting it means issuing a
	// new one.
	ErrTenantBudgetExceeded = errors.New("limes: tenant aggregate budget exceeded")

	ErrDelegationTooWide = errors.New("limes: child wider than parent")
	// ErrDelegationDepthExceeded — a Delegate whose child would have more
	// than MaxDelegationDepth ancestors. The parent stays valid; it is too
	// deep in its chain to delegate from, so the delegation is refused
	// (403) and nothing is recorded. It does not match ErrRevoked or
	// ErrDelegationTooDeep, which are the verify path's answers to a
	// lineage already too deep.
	ErrDelegationDepthExceeded = errors.New("limes: delegation would exceed the maximum depth")
	// ErrUnitCodeMismatch — two units that would have to be one: a
	// delegated child declaring a unit_code other than its parent's, or an
	// amount in a unit other than the one a counter (a capability's, an
	// ancestor's, a tenant's) already counts in. Nothing converts between
	// currencies, so cross-currency delegation is refused at issuance and a
	// cross-currency charge at the Meter. The request is well formed and
	// disagrees with what is on record, so it matches ErrConflict.
	ErrUnitCodeMismatch error = &familyError{"limes: unit_code mismatch", ErrConflict}
	// ErrInvalidRequest is a request malformed in itself: a missing tenant,
	// an empty audience entry, a negative TTL, a thumbprint that is not one,
	// a not-before past the expiry, caveats or an amount that do not
	// validate. Nothing was done. Every such error matches it, so a caller
	// maps the whole family to its "bad request" without listing it. A
	// request that is well formed but asks for more than is allowed has its
	// own sentinel instead: ErrDelegationTooWide, ErrUnitCodeMismatch.
	ErrInvalidRequest = errs.ErrInvalidRequest
	// ErrInvalidConfig is a component wired wrong: a constructor given a
	// config it cannot work with (a required field missing, a negative
	// bound), a key of another kind, or a dependency missing. Nothing was
	// built or done. It is the deployment's to fix, not the caller's, and is
	// answered 500 (docs/errors.md).
	ErrInvalidConfig = errs.ErrInvalidConfig
	// ErrInternal is an invariant of the module broken: a signature its own
	// key does not verify, a store answering otherwise than its contract
	// says. It is answered 500, the error's text, for the server's log,
	// naming what broke.
	ErrInternal = errs.ErrInternal
	// ErrUnknownTenant is an issuance for a tenant that does not exist —
	// typically one whose provisioning has not finished. The Store returns it.
	ErrUnknownTenant = errors.New("limes: unknown tenant")
	// ErrTenantDeleted is an issuance for a tenant in the trash: it exists,
	// so its rows may be restored, but nothing new is minted for it. The
	// Store returns it.
	ErrTenantDeleted = errors.New("limes: tenant deleted")
	// ErrTenantGone is an issuance for a tenant whose usage EraseTenantUsage
	// removed: nothing new is minted for it, and unlike ErrTenantDeleted
	// nothing of it can be restored (410). The Issuer returns it where the
	// Store refuses the record with ErrTenantErased, which it does not
	// match: that sentinel is a revoked capability's, and a mint presents
	// none.
	ErrTenantGone = errors.New("limes: tenant gone")
	// ErrScopeMismatch is a store call whose context is scoped to a tenant
	// other than the one its request names — or to none — under a store
	// that keeps each tenant's rows apart. The rows are there; the call may
	// not see them. It is the caller's wiring that is wrong, not the
	// request, so it matches neither ErrInvalidRequest nor ErrNotFound, and
	// ErrorResponse answers it 500.
	ErrScopeMismatch = errors.New("limes: call scoped to another tenant than its request names")
	// ErrProofUnsupported is a key-bound capability presented to a verifier
	// with no DPoP configured: no proof the client sends could be checked.
	// It is the deployment's fault, not the request's, so it matches no
	// ErrUnauthenticated sentinel and ErrorResponse invites no retry.
	ErrProofUnsupported = errors.New("limes: key-bound capability, and this verifier checks no proof")
	// ErrRevocationUnavailable is a revocation lookup that failed — the
	// store or the upstream that answers it unreachable, or failing — so
	// whether the capability is revoked is unknown. The verifier and the
	// issuer refuse with it, wrapping the lookup's own error, as the
	// verifier refuses a token whose issuer's keys cannot be fetched
	// (jwks.ErrUnavailable): a dependency failed, not the token, so it
	// matches no ErrUnauthenticated sentinel, and is answered 503, to retry.
	// A lookup's error that is a code of limes's already — a lineage too
	// deep (ErrDelegationTooDeep), a store's broken invariant
	// (ErrInternal) — keeps that code, but for ErrStoreUnavailable and
	// ErrStoreTimeout, which it wraps like any other failure.
	ErrRevocationUnavailable = errors.New("limes: revocation status unavailable")
)
```

Errors exposed to callers, which switch on them with errors.Is. A consumer maps them to its transport, or lets Verifier.ErrorResponse map them to HTTP.

Some are families that more specific sentinels match as well, so a caller branches on the one it needs:

	ErrUnauthenticated       the presented credentials were refused (401)
	├── ErrNoCredentials     none were presented
	├── ErrInvalidToken      the token is not genuine, or not this verifier's
	│   └── ErrBiscuitAttenuation
	├── ErrProofOfPossession the proof of possession is missing or wrong
	│   └── ErrAuthSchemeMismatch
	├── ErrRevoked
	│   └── ErrDelegationTooDeep, ErrTenantErased
	├── ErrUnrecorded        no record (unless VerifierConfig.AllowUnrecorded)
	└── ErrExpired, ErrNotYetValid, ErrAudienceMismatch
	ErrCaveatViolation       a caveat refuses the operation (403)
	ErrBudgetExceeded, ErrTenantBudgetExceeded, ErrRequestLimitExceeded
	                         a ceiling refuses the request (403)
	ErrInvalidRequest        the request itself is malformed
	├── ErrInvalidCaveats, ErrInvalidAmount, ErrEffectConflict
	└── ErrMalformedAuthorization  the client's Authorization header (400)
	ErrDelegationTooWide, ErrDelegationDepthExceeded
	                         a delegation its parent cannot grant (403)
	ErrNotFound              what the request names is not on record
	└── meter.ErrChargeNotFound, meter.ErrUsageNotFound, …
	ErrUnknownTenant, ErrTenantDeleted, ErrTenantGone
	                         an issuance for a tenant not open for one
	ErrConflict              a well-formed request disagrees with what is on record
	└── ErrAlreadyExists, ErrUnitCodeMismatch, meter.ErrExternalRefConflict, …

<a id="limes.ErrStoreUnavailable"></a><a id="limes.ErrStoreTimeout"></a>

### limes.ErrStoreUnavailable, limes.ErrStoreTimeout

```go
var (
	// ErrStoreUnavailable is a store that could not serve the call and may
	// serve it again: no connection to it, one it dropped before its answer
	// to a call that wrote nothing, the database shutting down or starting,
	// out of resources, or a transaction it aborted over a conflict another
	// one won. A call that wrote and whose commit went unanswered is never
	// this: its outcome is unknown (meter.ErrOutcomeUnknown), and sending it
	// again could apply it twice. Answered 503, to retry.
	ErrStoreUnavailable = errors.New("limes: store unavailable")
	// ErrStoreTimeout is a statement the store cancelled past its own
	// limit — PostgreSQL's statement_timeout or lock_timeout — the caller's
	// context still live. It wrote nothing. Answered 504, to retry.
	ErrStoreTimeout = errors.New("limes: store timed out")
)
```

A store's own failures, which a store wraps its driver's error in so that a caller answers each by its code rather than as an error of its own: the driver's error stays in the chain, for the log and for errors.As.

<a id="limes.Category"></a>

### limes.Category

```go
type Category string
```

Category is what a caller does about an error, coarser than its Code: every code belongs to exactly one, so a consumer maps the categories onto its transport rather than every code (docs/errors.md, "Categories"). Every code of a category is answered within one class of HTTP status, the client's (4xx) or the server's (5xx), so whose fault an error is follows from its category. Categories are never renamed; new ones may be added.

<a id="limes.CategoryUnauthenticated"></a><a id="limes.CategoryDenied"></a><a id="limes.CategoryExhausted"></a><a id="limes.CategoryInvalid"></a><a id="limes.CategoryNotFound"></a><a id="limes.CategoryConflict"></a><a id="limes.CategoryAlreadyExists"></a><a id="limes.CategoryPrecondition"></a><a id="limes.CategoryUnavailable"></a><a id="limes.CategoryInternal"></a>

#### limes.CategoryUnauthenticated, limes.CategoryDenied, limes.CategoryExhausted, limes.CategoryInvalid, limes.CategoryNotFound, limes.CategoryConflict, limes.CategoryAlreadyExists, limes.CategoryPrecondition, limes.CategoryUnavailable, limes.CategoryInternal

```go
const (
	// CategoryUnauthenticated — the credential is missing, unproven or no
	// longer good: present another. One the request carries malformed is
	// CategoryInvalid.
	CategoryUnauthenticated Category = "unauthenticated"
	// CategoryDenied — the credential is good and does not allow the
	// request.
	CategoryDenied Category = "denied"
	// CategoryExhausted — a request, budget, copy or lease limit, or the
	// DPoP proof quota of a replay window, refused it.
	CategoryExhausted Category = "exhausted"
	// CategoryInvalid — the request itself is wrong: sent again unchanged,
	// it fails again.
	CategoryInvalid Category = "invalid"
	// CategoryNotFound — what the request names is not on record.
	CategoryNotFound Category = "not_found"
	// CategoryConflict — the request disagrees with what is on record: read
	// it again, and decide.
	CategoryConflict Category = "conflict"
	// CategoryAlreadyExists — what the request would create is on record
	// already: read it rather than create it again.
	CategoryAlreadyExists Category = "already_exists"
	// CategoryPrecondition — the request is well formed, and the state it
	// needs is not on record: the ledger's room, the charge it refunds, or
	// another capability's lease. Sent again it fails again until that state
	// changes, which is no retry's to change. Always a 4xx: a server's own
	// configuration is CategoryInternal.
	CategoryPrecondition Category = "precondition"
	// CategoryUnavailable — a dependency failed on this request — did not
	// answer, or answered a page it had already given: retry later.
	CategoryUnavailable Category = "unavailable"
	// CategoryInternal — the server's configuration or a store failed: the
	// server's to fix. A feature the server does not run — leasing, a
	// proof checker — is its configuration too.
	CategoryInternal Category = "internal"
)
```

<a id="limes.CategoryOf"></a>

#### limes.CategoryOf

```go
func CategoryOf(err error) (Category, bool)
```

CategoryOf returns err's category, and false when err is no error of limes's, as CodeOf does. The meter's and the exchange's errors are limes's: one registry answers every code.

<sub>[category.go](../../category.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.CategoryOfCode"></a>

#### limes.CategoryOfCode

```go
func CategoryOfCode(code Code) (Category, bool)
```

CategoryOfCode returns code's category, and false for a code not among Codes: this package's, the meter's and, once module exchange is linked in, the exchange's. A consumer proving its own mapping of codes reads it beside Codes.

<a id="limes.Code"></a>

### limes.Code

```go
type Code string
```

Code is a stable, machine-readable name for any error limes returns (docs/adr/0012-error-codes.md, docs/errors.md): what a consumer puts on its wire, so a client branches on it rather than on a message, whose text is never a contract. A refusal of a presented capability has its Reason as its code; an error that Reason folds into a wider one keeps a code of its own (tenant\_erased, reported as revoked). Codes are never renamed; new ones may be added.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.CodeInvalidClient"></a><a id="limes.CodeUnauthorizedClient"></a><a id="limes.CodeUnsupportedGrantType"></a><a id="limes.CodeInvalidGrant"></a><a id="limes.CodeInvalidTarget"></a><a id="limes.CodeInvalidScope"></a><a id="limes.CodeInvalidAuthorizationDetails"></a><a id="limes.CodeServerError"></a>

#### limes.CodeInvalidClient, limes.CodeUnauthorizedClient, limes.CodeUnsupportedGrantType, limes.CodeInvalidGrant, limes.CodeInvalidTarget, limes.CodeInvalidScope, limes.CodeInvalidAuthorizationDetails, limes.CodeServerError

```go
const (
	CodeInvalidClient               Code = "invalid_client"
	CodeUnauthorizedClient          Code = "unauthorized_client"
	CodeUnsupportedGrantType        Code = "unsupported_grant_type"
	CodeInvalidGrant                Code = "invalid_grant"
	CodeInvalidTarget               Code = "invalid_target"
	CodeInvalidScope                Code = "invalid_scope"
	CodeInvalidAuthorizationDetails Code = "invalid_authorization_details"
	CodeServerError                 Code = "server_error"
)
```

The codes of module exchange's sentinels (docs/errors.md, "The exchange's codes"): the names RFC 6749 §5.2, RFC 8707 and RFC 9396 give them, which the token endpoint answers with. exchange.ErrInvalidRequest is CodeInvalidRequest. Each sentinel carries its own status, title and category, and the exchange registers them (internal/errcode): this package answers them from the sentinels, not from a table of its own, so the exchange adds a code without a release of limes.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.CodeOf"></a>

#### limes.CodeOf

```go
func CodeOf(err error) (Code, bool)
```

CodeOf returns err's code, and false when err is no error of limes's — nil, or a store's or the consumer's own — which a consumer answers as its own failure.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Codes"></a>

#### limes.Codes

```go
func Codes() []Code
```

Codes returns every code this package answers, each once: its own, the meter's and, once module exchange is linked in, the exchange's, so a consumer can prove its own mapping covers them all. The order is no contract: it may change in any release.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.DetailCodes"></a>

#### limes.DetailCodes

```go
func DetailCodes() []Code
```

DetailCodes are the codes whose problem may carry a Detail (ProblemOf): refusals of what the client sent — a request, its caveats, an amount, a delegation wider than its parent.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrorResponse"></a>

### limes.ErrorResponse

```go
type ErrorResponse struct {
	// Status is the HTTP status.
	Status int
	// Challenges are the WWW-Authenticate values, one per scheme; none for a
	// refusal that is not about authentication.
	Challenges []string
	// DPoPNonce is the nonce to send in the DPoP-Nonce header, when the
	// refusal asks for one. A use_dpop_nonce challenge always comes with it:
	// when the nonce cannot be given, the refusal is answered as the
	// server's failure instead (RFC 9449 §9).
	DPoPNonce string
	// Problem is the body.
	Problem Problem
}
```

ErrorResponse is how to answer a refused request.

<sub>[challenge.go](../../challenge.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Problem"></a>

### limes.Problem

```go
type Problem struct {
	// Type is a URI naming the kind of problem, after a fixed base
	// (ProblemTypeURI): a refusal's Reason, or for a refusal with none the
	// family it belongs to; for any other error, its Code.
	Type string `json:"type"`
	// Title is a short, fixed summary of the kind.
	Title string `json:"title"`
	// Status repeats the HTTP status.
	Status int `json:"status"`
	// Detail explains this occurrence, in terms safe to show the client:
	// set by ProblemOf, for a code of DetailCodes, as a constant naming the
	// part of the request refused and the rule it broke, never a value.
	Detail string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
	// Reason is the refusal's Reason, an extension member (RFC 9457 §3.2):
	// the stable name a client branches on, which the Type URI ends with.
	// Empty for a refusal with none.
	Reason Reason `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	// Code is the error's Code, an extension member: its Reason, or the
	// narrower code Reason folds into it (docs/errors.md).
	Code Code `json:"code,omitempty"`
	// Category is the Code's Category, an extension member: what the caller
	// does about the error, for a consumer mapping its transport from the
	// problem alone.
	Category Category `json:"category,omitempty"`
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Problem is an RFC 9457 problem details object.

<sub>[challenge.go](../../challenge.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ProblemFor"></a>

#### limes.ProblemFor

```go
func ProblemFor(err error) Problem
```

ProblemFor is ProblemOf for any error: one that is not limes's — a store's own failure, a consumer's — is answered as internal, 500, so every error a consumer passes has a code and a body.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ProblemOf"></a>

#### limes.ProblemOf

```go
func ProblemOf(err error) (Problem, bool)
```

ProblemOf is the RFC 9457 problem details of err, an error limes returned, for a consumer's own API, whatever its transport: its type URI, a fixed title, its HTTP status, its code, its category and, for a refusal, its Reason. A refusal's is the body Verifier.ErrorResponse writes. False for an error that is not limes's: answer that as the server's failure.

Its Detail is set for a refusal of the client's own input — a code of DetailCodes — when the refusal says which part of the request it refused and which rule that broke, and is empty otherwise. A detail is written where the refusal is, as a constant: it never holds an id, a key id, an issuer, a tenant, a resource or any other value — the client's or the server's. The error's text, which may name all of those, is for the server's log alone.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ProblemOfCode"></a>

#### limes.ProblemOfCode

```go
func ProblemOfCode(code Code) (Problem, bool)
```

ProblemOfCode is the problem ProblemOf answers an error with code with, and false for a code not among Codes: a consumer holding only a code, or pinning the contract its mapping was written against (limestest), reads it without an error to hand.

<sub>[code.go](../../code.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Reason"></a>

### limes.Reason

```go
type Reason string
```

Reason is a stable, machine-readable name for why a presented capability was refused. The sentinels stay the way to branch in Go; a Reason is what a consumer puts on the wire, so that a client in any language tells "this capability is spent" from "this request was malformed" without reading a message. The values are never renamed; new ones may be added.

The refusals a verifier, Caveats.Check or a meter.Meter returns for a presented capability.

<sub>[reason.go](../../reason.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ReasonOf"></a>

#### limes.ReasonOf

```go
func ReasonOf(err error) (Reason, bool)
```

ReasonOf returns the reason err refused a capability for, and false when err is no such refusal — nil, a store failure, or a programming error such as ErrInvalidRequest, which a consumer maps as it maps any other. The one member of that family that is a refusal, ErrMalformedAuthorization, has its reason.

<sub>[reason.go](../../reason.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ReasonOfCode"></a>

#### limes.ReasonOfCode

```go
func ReasonOfCode(code Code) (Reason, bool)
```

ReasonOfCode returns the reason a refusal with code is challenged with — its own name, or the wider one it is folded into, as tenant\_erased into revoked, or copy\_limit\_exceeded into request\_limit\_exceeded — and false for a code that is no refusal, such as not\_found.

<sub>[reason.go](../../reason.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Reasons"></a>

#### limes.Reasons

```go
func Reasons() []Reason
```

Reasons returns every reason this package defines, in a fixed order, so a consumer can prove its own mapping covers them all.

<sub>[reason.go](../../reason.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Reason.Permanent"></a>

#### limes.Reason.Permanent

```go
func (r Reason) Permanent() bool
```

Permanent reports whether a refusal for r stands for as long as the capability does: the same request with the same capability will be refused again, whatever happens elsewhere, so a caller stops rather than retries.

A refusal that something else can lift is not permanent: a budget frees as holds lapse or charges are refunded, a tenant ceiling is raised by an operator, a taint flag is cleared, a not-yet-valid capability becomes valid, a proof is signed afresh, the verifier fetches its keys again or reaches its revocations, and an idempotency key can be added to the request.
